spec.status: HYPOTHESIS: unvalidated until rows are added to partial_gravity_validation.csv
spec.idea: In microgravity the only airflow is the forced flow NASA sets. On the Moon and Mars, buoyancy adds its own weak flow around the flame. The bridge adds a buoyant velocity scale to the forced flow and then reads the ISS-trained outcome model at that effective airflow.
spec.equation: u_buoyant = u_ref * (g / g_earth)^n ;  u_effective = sqrt(u_forced^2 + u_buoyant^2)
assumptions: u_ref (buoyant flow scale at 1 g for a flame of NASA-test size) is NOT measured in this project. It is a prior range, 10 to 30 cm/s, shown to the user and adjustable.
n between 1/3 and 1/2 spans two textbook buoyancy scalings (diffusive and free-fall); the truth for these flames is not established here.
Forced and buoyant flows are combined as a magnitude only. Direction (concurrent, opposed) is carried over from the forced flow, which is a simplification.
The ISS-trained model is read at the effective flow as if airflow were airflow. Real partial-gravity flames can differ in shape, soot and radiation, which this ignores.
Pressure and material are not model inputs, so the bridge cannot reflect them.

derivation.note: Standard free-fall dimensional estimate of buoyant velocity over a length L. L stands for the flame height or standoff scale and is an ASSUMPTION (0.1 to 1 cm here), not measured in this project. The 10 to 30 cm/s prior is this estimate rounded; it is not taken from a NASA measurement.

validation.note: No partial-gravity results have been added, so the bridge is a hypothesis only.
